block_node.block_desc: Propagate signals from one point in space to multiple points or from multiple points back to one point. The block models propagation time, free-space propagation loss, and Doppler shift. The block assumes that the propagation speed is much greater than the object's speed in which case the stop-and-hop model is valid.

Propagate signals from one point in space to multiple points or from multiple points back to one point. The block can propagate wideband signals by dividing them into subbands. The block models propagation time, free-space propagation loss, and Doppler shift. The block assumes that the propagation speed is much greater than the object's speed in which case the stop-and-hop model is valid.

Compute the signal echo according to the specified radar cross-section (RCS) or scattering matrix (when polarization is enabled). The target supports all four Swerling models. Several targets can be modeled by specifying a vector of RCS's.

Compute the reflected signal off a backscatter target according to the specified radar cross-section (RCS) or scattering matrix (when polarization is enabled). The target supports all four Swerling models. Several targets can be modeled by specifying multiple RCS patterns.

Compute the reflected wideband signal off a backscatter target according to the specified radar cross-section (RCS) or scattering matrix (when polarization is enabled). The target supports all four Swerling models. The block can simulate wideband signals by dividing them into subbands. Several targets can be modeled by specifying a cell array of RCS patterns.

Propagate signals from one point in space to multiple points or from multiple points back to one point via line of sight channels. The block models propagation time, free-space propagation loss, Doppler shift, and atmospheric as well as weather loss. The block assumes that the propagation speed is much greater than the object's speed in which case the stop-and-hop model is valid.

Propagate signals from one point in space to multiple points or from multiple points back to one point via line of sight channels. The block can propagate wideband signals by dividing them into subbands. The block models propagation time, free-space propagation loss, Doppler shift, and atmospheric as well as weather loss. The block assumes that the propagation speed is much greater than the object's speed in which case the stop-and-hop model is valid.

Propagate signals through a 3D scattering based MIMO channel defined by a transmit array, a receive array, and a number of scatterers. Each scatterer defines a path. The transmitted signals travel along each path before they arrive at the receive array
Calculate the range (in meters) or azimuth and elevation angles (in degrees) of several positions with respect to a reference. The reference position could be specified in the dialog or as an input.

Model the motion of platforms such as airplanes or ground vehicles. Platforms can be configured using either constant velocity or constant acceleration models. The orientation of the platforms can also be specified.
Conversion between azimuth and broadside angles.
